Subject: POC plan & timeline — kickoff, weekly check-ins, success criteria

Hi Tom and Sara,

Great to speak with you both earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through the evaluation goals. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed POC plan and next steps so we have alignment before we lock in dates.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood inference for Acme’s customer-facing summarization workflow (250–1,000 tokens, 99th-pct latency target ~350ms).

Proposed success criteria (attached: Redwood_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx)
- Precision: model reaches ≥ 0.88 accuracy on Acme’s 200-sample labeled set (business-defined measure)
- Latency: median latency < 250ms, 95th pct < 450ms for target payloads
- Cost: per-invocation inference cost within agreed band (we’ll provide estimates once we see sample volume)
- Integration: end-to-end integration with Acme’s staging API (OAuth SSO + IP allowlist)

POC timeline (proposal)
- Kickoff: week of Mar 22 (technical + success-criteria walkthrough) — 60 min
- Week 1–4: weekly 30-min check-ins to review data ingestion, initial runs, and metrics
- Final readout: Apr 30 — 45–60 min demo + results and next-steps

Ownership
- Acme: provide labeled sample set (200 items), staging API access, engineering lead for integration (Sara)
- Redwood: provide test harness, dedicated SE (Vivek) for onboarding, weekly metric reports (Marissa)

Action items / asks for this week
1) Can you confirm the kickoff week — we currently proposed Mar 22 (Mon) but flexible if that doesn’t work
2) Please share the labeled sample set and SSO/IP requirements by Mar 17
3) Let me know any internal stakeholders we should include on the kickoff invite

I’ve attached the success-criteria worksheet and a sample POC agenda. Happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

Hi Tom / Sara — Vivek from Redwood (SE) here. Quick technical notes to help planning:

- Staging options: either we ingest via secure S3 (preferred for dataset uploads) or we can hit your staging API if you want end-to-end latency numbers. S3 is faster to get started.
- For SSO/API access we’ll need a short-lived service account and an allowlisted set of IPs; I’ll send the IP range separately.
- For the kickoff I recommend two agenda items: (1) success criteria & evaluation plan, (2) integration checklist / sample request payload. 30–45 min should be enough for the tech portion.
- Sample prompts and expected output format (JSON schema) will help us wire the test harness quickly — can you share examples in the export?

I’ll block time for Mar 24 at 10am PT tentatively until we hear final confirmation.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
